notes: §1985:XIII.3.22.3 SR1: 'A signed numeric literal must have associated with it a signed numeric PICTURE character-string.' ValidateNumericValue refuses a signed literal on an unsigned subject (COBOL1625, the witness PIC 9 VALUE -5); the 2023 widening to a sign-bearing numeric-edited subject cannot reach 85, because ScreenNumericEditedNumericLiteral refuses any numeric literal on a numeric-edited report item below 2023 (COBOL0900, matching §1985:XIII.3.22.4 GR1 b's 'must be a nonnumeric literal'), and ValidateValueCategory refuses a numeric literal on an alphanumeric item (COBOL1657). Probes (std 85): b) PIC 9 VALUE +5 and VALUE -5 COBOL1625; PIC -9 VALUE -5 and PIC Z9 VALUE 5 COBOL0900; PIC X(2) VALUE -5 COBOL1657; PIC 9(3) VALUE ALL "1" COBOL1657; d) PIC S9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE VALUE -5 printed -5, SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE VALUE +5 printed 5+, unsigned 5 into a signed item printed +5, PIC S9 (no SIGN, implementor-defined per §1985:XIII.3.17.4 GR2) VALUE -5 printed the overpunch N, scaled S9V9 VALUE -1.5 printed -15, SPP9 VALUE -.005 printed -5, ZERO printed 000, ZEROS on S9(3) printed +000; f) S9(18) VALUE -999999999999999999 printed all 18 digits with the sign; a, e: not reachable (report items have no OCCURS DEPENDING ON or file arm at 85).

next.reason: §1985:XIII.3.22.3 SR1: 'A signed numeric literal must have associated with it a signed numeric PICTURE character-string'; a numeric-edited report item took only a nonnumeric literal (§1985:XIII.3.22.4 GR1 b). §2023:13.18.63.3 SR3 lets the subject be 'either a signed numeric data item or a numeric-edited data item with a representation of a sign', and §2023:13.18.63.3 SR6 lets numeric literals be used for numeric-edited items in formats 1, 2 and 4 (format 4 is the report section). A signed numeric literal for a signed numeric-edited report item, refused in 1985, is accepted: looser. Compile-time in both.
